own_solution.law: Joule heating in an ohmic resistor: P = V^2 / R
assumptions: 12.0 V is the voltage across the resistor itself
resistance is 8.0 ohm at operating conditions

defect_reasons.invalid_numerical_precision: The certified answer is displayed as 20 W, but V^2/R = 144/8 = 18 W exactly; rounding to one significant figure (an 11% error) is far coarser than the 2-3 significant-figure inputs and makes the displayed answer wrong.

counterexamples: With V = 12.0 V and R = 8.0 ohm, P = 18.0 W; a solver answering 18 W would be scored against a certified 20 W and could be marked wrong under any tolerance tighter than about 11%.
notes: Governing equation P = V^2/R and parameters match the problem; units are consistent (V^2/ohm = W). The invariance claim is correct: ambient pressure (18-144 kPa) has no physical path to P when V and R are specified, so all renderings share the same answer and differ only in the pressure value. The only defect is the certified answer display of 20 W instead of 18 W. If the stored certified value is 18 W and only the display is rounded, the fix is to display 18 W (or 18.0 W). Agrees with my pass 1 (18 W, pressure disconnected); the change in validity is due solely to the certified answer display seen in pass 2.
